subject: EdgeVault on-prem plan: ephemeral GPU scratch strategy & cold-archive separation
messages:
From: Anders Lund <anders@edgevault.io>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private cluster questions on scratch/arch split

Camila/Marissa — thanks again for the intro call. A few follow-ups from our infra team as we sketch the on-prem topology: 

1) We expect heavy short-lived GPU workloads (model training-ish inference) that must use local NVMe scratch for performance, but we also need a separate cold archive that sits on encrypted network attached block storage (retention 3y). Any recommendations for node class separation, PVC binding, and data-movement guarantees?

2) Our security team requires proof of immutable cold storage snapshots and key separation (KMS + customer HSM). Can Redwood outline the recommended backup/restore pattern and what we need to provide on our side?

3) Network: default proposal is a VPC-per-cluster with dedicated NAT egress, restricted peering to the control plane, and no direct internet from worker nodes. Are there gotchas (DNS, NTP, STUN/traces) that typically require exceptions?

Attaching our initial site inventory (small). Would like your pragmatic recommended node classes and an ops checklist so our SREs can provision hardware this week.

— Anders
EdgeVault Inc

Anders — thanks, useful context. Looping in Marissa for storage specifics, and Karthik for network gating. High level thoughts below; I can turn this into a short node-class + PV decision doc (xlsx + diagram) and drop in Drive.

Summary recommendations (short):
- Node classes:
  * gpu-scratch (local NVMe, ephemeral): for low-latency model workloads. Use kubelet local storage with hostPath-managed scratch volumes and NodeAffinity to pin pods.
  * compute-general (ssd): general inference/transform jobs, use CSI-attached block volumes (encrypted).
  * archive-attach (hdd/large blockstore): no GPUs, long-term retention volumes mounted read-only to clients via CSI snapshots/volume clones for exports.

- Storage flow:
  1) Workloads write to local NVMe (ephemeral) during runtime.
  2) Periodic checkpoint/flush job copies finalized artifacts to CSI-backed encrypted volumes in archive-attach (cronJob + rsync or parallelized copy operator).
  3) Archive volumes snapshot to customer-controlled KMS/HSM-backed snapshots nightly; retention policy enforced by SRE-run lifecycle jobs.

- Backup/restore & compliance:
  * Use CSI snapshots + offsite object export (if policy requires immutability) to an object store that supports WORM or signed manifests.
  * Redwood can trigger snapshots but we need customer KMS access or envelope keys for HSM signing.
  * Documented restore playbook: restore snapshot -> attach to staging nodeclass -> validate checksums -> promote.

- Network items:
  * DNS/NTP: allow worker egress to your internal DNS/NTP endpoints. If blocking internet, ensure control plane and container registries reachable via proxy.
  * Egress for telemetry: allow outbound to Redwood control plane endpoints (cidr list) for health-checking and optional metrics.

I'll produce the attachment with node-class sizing and an ops checklist. Meeting tomorrow to walk through? Proposed 2026-02-11 10:00 PT.

— Camila

Anders — quick storage notes from my side:

Operational guarantees we recommend:
- Local NVMe scratch: treat as ephemeral — don't rely on it for long-lived data. Ensure pods checkpoint every 10-30 minutes depending on workload.
- Use CSI driver that supports VolumeSnapshotContent (snapshot class policy) and enforce server-side encryption at-rest.
- Archive export: use blockstore-backed volumes with snapshot lifecycle. For immutability, add an export path to an object store (minio/S3) with signed manifests; include manifest to prove provenance.

Suggested PV policy (high level):
- gpu-scratch: StorageClass: local-nvme; reclaimPolicy: Retain (so ops can inspect after pod eviction) + backup job to copy to temp-project PVC before deletion.
- archive-attach: StorageClass: blockstore-encrypted; snapshotClass: encrypted-snap; retention policy enforced in object-store and in cluster.

Attachments: I put a draft node-classes worksheet in Drive (edgevault_node_classes_v1.xlsx) and a simple lifecycle diagram (storage_lifecycle_diagram.png). Will include a SOW outline in the same folder.

— Marissa
Principal Cloud Ops, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: 2026-02-11T09:05:00-08:00

Network gotchas to call out before provisioning hardware: 

- Egress pinholes: If you lock outbound, you must permit: container registry endpoints, Redwood controlplane IPs (I listed these in Drive link), and your internal NTP/DNS. Also allow CRI runtime checks to update images on boot.
- MTU and jumbo frames: NVMe over fabric or remote blockstore can require consistent MTU; confirm top-of-rack and switch config.
- BGP/Anycast: If you want regional failover with multiple racks, we'll need predictable egress IPs for service-level routing.
- Firewall rules: recommend a dedicated subnet for archive-attach with stricter egress; gpu-scratch nodes can have limited outgoing access but must be able to reach the archive gateway over encrypted path for flush jobs.

I'll add a minimal iptables/Calico policy example to Drive. Also note: DNS resolvers inside the VPC should return internal service FQDNs for control plane endpoints.

— Karthik
